question: What is the medical definition of a fracture?

options.A: A stretching injury to the ligaments surrounding a joint
options.B: A complete break or crack in the continuity of a bone
options.C: An infection located deep inside the bone marrow
options.D: A sudden tear in the muscle fibers attached to bone

explanation: A fracture simply means the physical structure of the bone has cracked or broken due to stress or trauma. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h1)

question: How does an open fracture differ from a closed fracture?

options.A: Open fractures have a skin wound communicating with the break
options.B: Closed fractures involve multiple pieces of shattered bone
options.C: Closed fractures always require immediate surgical metal plating
options.D: Open fractures only occur in elderly patients with weak bones

explanation: The defining feature of an open fracture is a break in the skin that exposes the bone directly to the outside air. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is a pathologic fracture?

options.A: A break occurring in a bone weakened by an underlying disease
options.B: A minor hairline crack caused by repetitive athletic training
options.C: A clean break resulting from a high-speed motor vehicle crash
options.D: A fracture caused strictly by a direct blow from a blunt object

explanation: Pathologic fractures happen because an existing disease like cancer or osteoporosis has already made the bone fragile. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which patient has the highest risk for developing a fragility fracture?

options.A: A healthy young adult who plays competitive contact football
options.B: An elderly woman with long-standing postmenopausal osteoporosis
options.C: A middle-aged man with a history of mild muscular sprains
options.D: A teenage athlete recovering from a minor hamstring strain

explanation: Osteoporosis severely decreases bone mass, making minor movements or low-impact falls sufficient to cause a severe break. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the term for the grating sound heard when broken bone ends rub together?
explanation: Crepitus is the distinctive crunchy sound or sensation produced when rough ends of fractured bone rub together. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check the pulse and skin color below a fractured limb?

options.A: To check for signs of blood vessel or nerve damage
options.B: To calculate the exact date when the bone will heal
options.C: To prevent the development of a systemic bone infection
options.D: To determine how much calcium the patient's body needs

explanation: Swelling or displaced bone fragments can pinch nearby arteries and nerves, cutting off blood supply and sensation to the fingers or toes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of immediate first aid for a suspected fracture?

options.A: Push any protruding bone ends back inside the skin
options.B: Apply hot packs to the injury site to reduce swelling
options.C: Straighten the deformed limb immediately by pulling hard
options.D: Immobilize the bone to prevent further tissue damage

explanation: Keeping the broken bone still stops sharp edges from tearing nearby blood vessels, nerves, and muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h4)

question: A patient has an open fracture with a small piece of bone sticking out of the skin. What is the correct initial nursing action?

options.A: Wash the exposed bone vigorously with strong antiseptic soap and water
options.B: Straighten the limb forcefully to hide the bone before taking an X-ray
options.C: Push the bone back inside the wound quickly and apply a tight tourniquet
options.D: Cover the wound loosely with a sterile dressing without pushing the bone in

explanation: Manipulating or pushing exposed bone back inside introduces deep infection, so the area must be covered loosely and left for the surgical team. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h4)

question: What does the term 'reduction' mean in the management of fractures?

options.A: Gradual shrinking of local soft tissue swelling using ice packs
options.B: Lowering the patient's blood pressure prior to orthopedic surgery
options.C: Surgical removal of dead bone tissue from an infected site
options.D: Realignment of the broken bone fragments into their normal position

explanation: Reduction is the process of putting displaced bone ends back into their correct anatomical alignment so they can heal properly. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why might a surgeon choose external fixation over a standard internal plate for a severe open fracture?

options.A: It allows the patient to remove the metal pins at home every evening
options.B: It avoids placing metal hardware directly into a contaminated wound area
options.C: It completely eliminates any need for follow-up X-ray imaging
options.D: It guarantees that the bone will heal twice as fast as internal surgery

explanation: External frames hold bones securely from the outside, minimizing the risk of trapping bacteria and deep infection inside a dirty open wound. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which symptom is the earliest and most reliable indicator of developing compartment syndrome?

options.A: Complete lack of any pulse felt in the foot or hand
options.B: Blue discoloration of the skin spreading rapidly over the toes
options.C: Severe, relentless pain that is not relieved by opioid pain medication
options.D: Total paralysis of all the fingers and toes on the affected limb

explanation: Intense, out-of-proportion pain that fails to respond to strong painkillers is the hallmark early warning sign of rising pressure inside a muscle compartment. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary mechanism behind a fat embolism following a long bone fracture?

options.A: Immobility causes fat cells under the skin to melt into the bloodstream
options.B: Infection at the fracture site turns local soft tissues into fatty deposits
options.C: The body stores extra dietary fat in broken bones during the healing phase
options.D: Fat droplets from the bone marrow enter open blood vessels and travel to the lungs

explanation: When a large long bone breaks, yellow bone marrow fat can escape into damaged blood vessels, creating emboli that block small vessels in the lungs and brain. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the correct way to handle a newly applied plaster cast while it is still drying?

options.A: Lift the cast using only the fingertips
options.B: Support the cast using the palms of the hands
options.C: Rest the damp cast on a narrow, hard metal bar
options.D: Wrap the cast tightly in thick plastic sheeting

explanation: Fingertips create flat pressure spots on a drying plaster cast, which can indent the plaster and cause skin breakdown underneath. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h7)

question: A patient with a leg cast complains of severe itching deep inside the cast. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Tell the patient to pour warm water down the cast to wash away the itchy skin cells
options.B: Cut the cast off immediately because itching means a severe infection is present
options.C: Instruct the patient never to insert objects inside and suggest using a cool hair dryer setting
options.D: Provide a long knitting needle wrapped in cotton gauze so they can scratch safely

explanation: Foreign objects can break fragile skin inside the cast and introduce bacteria, while cool air safely relieves itching without harming the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h7)
